symbols.name: source set
symbols.meaning: The set of inputs of the map $f$, each of which $f$ sends to an element of $W$.
symbols.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

symbols.name: target set
symbols.meaning: The set that the map $f$ sends its inputs into, the set of outputs.
symbols.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

symbols.name: map
symbols.meaning: The map from the source set $U$ to the target set $W$ whose bijectivity is tested.
symbols.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

symbols.name: source element
symbols.meaning: An element of the source set $U$, the input of the map $f$.
symbols.quote: Let $U$ and $W$ be sets, the source set $U$ and the target set $W$, and let $f\colon U\to W$ be a map, which sends each element $\sigma$ of $U$ to an element $f(\sigma)$ of $W$.

symbols.name: target element
symbols.meaning: An element of the target set $W$, the output that a bijection must hit exactly once.
symbols.quote: - onto: for every $\xi\in W$ there is some $\sigma\in U$ with $f(\sigma)=\xi$, so every target is hit.

symbols.name: padded address set
symbols.meaning: A set of integer addresses on which a tape procedure acts, including its padding.
symbols.quote: Its padded address set $\Gamma$ is a set of integer addresses on which the step acts.

symbols.name: non-example map
symbols.meaning: The map $\sigma\mapsto\lfloor\sigma/2\rfloor$ on $\{0,1,2,3\}$, which is not a bijection.
symbols.quote: A non-example is illustrated using the [Floor function](floor-function.md): the map $f_2(\sigma)=\lfloor \sigma/2\rfloor$ on the same sets is not a bijection, because $f_2(0)=f_2(1)=0$ and the targets $2$ and $3$ are never hit, so it has no inverse.

symbols.name: singled-out set
symbols.meaning: A subset of the source set $U$ singled out by the argument, which is where two bijections may differ: the bad addresses.
symbols.quote: For a subset $G\subseteq U$, the set of elements singled out by the argument, write $G^c=U\setminus G$ for its complement.

symbols.name: composed bijection
symbols.meaning: The bijection of the rectangle that the update lines of the interchange compose to.
symbols.quote: Two bijections of the rectangle, $S_0$ (the one its update lines compose to) and $T_0$ (the ideal one), agree outside $G$, the [Exceptional set](exceptional-set.md) of bad addresses, so they are compared on the complement of $G$.

symbols.name: ideal bijection
symbols.meaning: The ideal bijection of the rectangle that performs the required XORs and fixes the other coordinates.
symbols.quote: Two bijections of the rectangle, $S_0$ (the one its update lines compose to) and $T_0$ (the ideal one), agree outside $G$, the [Exceptional set](exceptional-set.md) of bad addresses, so they are compared on the complement of $G$.
